mantra.line: Logistics wins wars before the first shot. Every token not spent re-reading the board is a token spent on the front.
One function, two verbs: audit and improve. It never sleeps and it never grows a second head.
Adopt the audit standards for their shape, not their text. ISO 19011 is a pattern; the AAR is already in the Command's blood.

frago.mission: Stand up one standing audit-and-improvement function over every system in daily use, and move compute off the chat onto the harness, **in order to** make the whole operation cheaper per turn and better every week, so the fronts are supplied before the fight.
frago.order: **Rule the four open calls below in one breath, or say "defaults" and they lock as written.** The offload is built and proven live; what is left on this sheet is doctrine, not code.
frago.default: Silence: AAR + PDCA on the 19011 pattern stays the instrument; the function stays the logistics front; one AAR line inside every Oscar Mike plus a full pass weekly; sheets built from repo JSON republish only from the building session, and any cross-session republish pays the read (about 22–25k tokens) unless Papi says force.

paragraphs.name: Situation
paragraphs.plain: What you asked, what the numbers say, and what the register holds for this.

strand.last: The standards campaign (BOLO 50) landed its register 9/11.
strand.plan: Open the logistics front: audit + improve, and stop paying tokens for compute the harness can do.

items.t: **"This is theater warfare with multiple fronts, and this is a big one: the logistics front."** Not a side quest. Standardize the auditing and continuous-improvement process for everything in daily use.
**The token worry:** Claude Code shipped tooling not yet in use; the fear is overspend; the want is compute pushed onto side programs instead of the chat.
**Standards in every BOLO from here.** Pull the applicable ones from BOLO 50's register; boresight them against the live systems.

groups.label: Where the tokens went · measured 9/12 from the local transcripts

items.t: **Last eight days ≈ 53.6M weighted** (201M cache-read · 18M cache-write · 2.1M output). **9/10 alone was half the week.**
**Performer and creator research ≈ 51%** (the 9/8 register merge · the 9/10 creator cases, 16 agents · the 9/10 performer list). **Sit rep and page sessions ≈ 41%.** Everything else 8%.

**41 subagents = 35% of the week, all but four on Fable.** Tool results of the whole week ≈ 2.3M tokens: the scrape volume was not the cost, the agent contexts were. Five creator-case files never landed; that slice bought nothing.
**Correction to the first read:** the 211 KB session open is a steady tax (~13%), not the spike. The spikes were agent fleets and long sessions.
**The gauge is saved:** `_tools/usage/usage_by_day.py N` · `usage_by_agent.py`. Zero tokens to rerun.

**The session open is a steady tax, not the spike** (corrected after the transcript count). The reading order (SOP → STATE → BOLO → cache → PROJECTS) is 211 KB on disk, roughly 55,000 tokens read before the first order and re-read every turn: about 13% of the week. Still worth the digest.

**Pages are already cheap.** The DOPE SHEET and SITREP run template + JSON + build script; an update costs the JSON, not the HTML. The visual tools (the design canvas, Figma) do not make the first draft cheaper: the draft is still written by Claude. They make every tweak after it free, because you move things by hand instead of asking.

**Subagents do not cut the bill; they cut the context.** A read done by an Explore or haiku agent never enters this window, so every later turn stays light. Workflows spawn many agents and cost more, not less: audits only, like the 90-agent DARKROOM pass.
**Hooks cost nothing.** The autocommit Stop hook is the proof. A SessionStart hook can print the board opening from a script; a PostToolUse hook can rebuild a DOPE SHEET whenever its JSON changes.

groups.label: The standards pulled from the register · 9/12

items.t: **The quality core: ISO 9001:2015 clauses 9 and 10** (performance evaluation: monitoring, internal audit, management review · improvement: nonconformity, corrective action, continual improvement) with ISO/TS 9002 and the small-enterprise guide; **ISO 9004** for the self-assessment maturity grid. Paid text; the clause shape is public and is all the Command needs.

**The audit standard: ISO 19011** (guidelines for auditing management systems: the audit programme, the principles, auditor competence). The one document that describes the function you just ordered. ASQ's free overview covers the shape.

**Software and systems: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 + 15288** (quality assurance, verification, validation, configuration management, measurement, decision management as named processes) · **ISO/IEC 25021** quality-measure elements (25010's quality model sits beside it) · **29148** requirements, a register gap.

**The AI layer: ISO/IEC 42001 + 42005 + 42006** (AI management system · impact assessment · auditing the AI management system). The operation runs on an AI; 42001's resource and performance-monitoring controls are the token question in standards language.

**Risk and problem solving: ISO 31000 + IEC 31010** (the risk register every BOLO brief already implies) · **AIAG CQI-2021** effective problem solving (the 8D root-cause method) · **PMBOK 8** quality and lessons-learned · **ISO 10015 / 10018** competence and engagement, which is BVX-LEARN's clause.

**The Command-native instruments the register does not list, all free:** the **AAR** (After Action Review: what was planned, what happened, why, what to sustain, what to improve; the Army's and the Corps' own improvement standard) · **MCDP 7 Learning** (already organic as MIL.07) · **PDCA** (Deming's cycle, the spine of every ISO management standard) · the Toyota **A3** · **DMAIC**. Recommendation: AAR + PDCA are the working instruments; the ISO texts give the vocabulary and the clause map, never bought.
**For every page the Command publishes:** MIL-STD-1472H (organic via the WATCH register) and **WCAG 2.x**, the biggest gap in the register.

**A republish from a session that did not build the sheet is refused until the live page is fetched into context (~80 KB, about 65k tokens), and a second refusal can demand the fetch again.** Sheet 51 v0.3 hit it: built locally, republish owed. The FRAGO itself costs about 1 KB. This is the largest single token cost the offload build found, and it is the tool's, not the Command's.

paragraphs.name: Execution
paragraphs.plain: Offload first, because it pays for everything after. Then the audit register. Then the cadence.

strand.last: The offload build landed in one night on Papi's "permission granted, do all of it."
strand.plan: Six phases; the first three are cheap and mechanical.
strand.you: You ruled the offload 9/12 and it has now carried three live runs without you touching a file. The four doctrine calls are still yours.
strand.next: Rule the instrument, the name, the cadence, and the force order. Then the first manual audit pass, which unlocks pick f (the weekly cloud routine).

paragraphs.main_effort: The offload. Every phase after it is cheaper once it lands.

phases.t: **The consult** — where the tokens go, what the tools do, the standards pulled.
**The picks** — a–f RULED 9/12 ("permission granted, do all of it") and built. Still yours: the instrument, the function's name, the cadence, the force order.

**The offload build — RULED + BUILT 9/12 night on "permission granted, do all of it"**, as eight sub-phases under the formation (BOLO 54): every one a script for the zero-token half, a haiku or sonnet specialist only where reading needs judgment, a script reviewer at the fan-in, the main line writing one thing.

**The system boresight** — every system in daily use on one register: what it is · owner · the standard it answers to · last audit · open findings. The gate (first live runs) cleared 9/15–9/16 (phase 9); `collect.py` and the digest give the reads. Ready to run on your go.
**The first audit pass** — one AAR per system on the register; findings become BOLO rows or FRAGOs.
**The cadence** — a one-line AAR inside every Oscar Mike; the full pass on the chosen interval, as a cloud routine when ready.
**File on the ladder** — the audit standard and the register land on BOLO 50's Command ladder once it is ruled.

**2.1 · Session open** — `_tools/sitrep/digest.py` prints ~40 lines (rack · Blocked rows · newest BOLOs · PMCS red · box · tree · main effort · sizes on disk); wired as a SessionStart hook in `.claude/settings.local.json`. The five files open on demand only.

**2.2 · Oscar Mike** — `_tools/oscarmike/close.py` pulls the session's spoken turns from the local transcript and writes the NOTE brief (haiku drafts the Ready Rack note); `journal.py` appends the day's journal from the note; the main line rules the note and writes STATE's Moved bullet. Skill: `oscar-mike`.

**2.3 · FRAGO** — `_tools/bolostatus/frago.py N patch.json --build`: a ~1 KB patch (status · order · calls · phases · files · items · strand · log · related) merged onto the sheet, version bumped, built. No agent. This entry is its first live use. Skill: `frago`.

**2.4 · DOPE SHEET** — `_tools/bolostatus/prep.py N` gathers the row, the rows it names, STATE and note mentions, and the schema; SHEET (sonnet) drafts S · E · A · L; the main line writes M · C · the order and calls; `check.py N --promote` reviews; `build.py N`; publish. Skill: `dope-sheet`.

**2.5 · Creator research** — `_tools/creator-cases/fetch.py <slug> --fansly --x --ph --url`: script fetch (Fansly API · fxtwitter · Wayback via curl) into raw/ + manifest; EXTRACT (haiku) → facts.json; WRITE (sonnet) → the case file per case-brief.md; `check.py <slug>` reviews (ten sections · TTP · sources · privacy tripwires). **The runs stay HELD (Papi, 9/11); the formation is built.**

**2.6 · RTB** — `_tools/oscarmike/rtb_prep.py` compiles the 20 open cards with their resume lines; DISPO (haiku) proposes one disposition line per card; the main line rules the lines. Skill: `rtb`. **The rulings are Papi's; not fired.**

**2.7 · Collect (LOCI + the standards register)** — `_tools/loci/collect.py <locus.md> --limit --batch`: script fetch of every link to text + manifest; EXTRACT-k (haiku) per batch → extract.k.json; WRITE (sonnet) → the register; `check.py <name> <register.md>` proves every fetched link is covered. Skill: `collect`.
**2.8 · BOLO add** — `_tools/bolo/add.py "title" "body" --trunk --status`: next number, date, header stamp, glossary stub, the DOPE SHEET prep command printed. The wording stays the main line's.

**First live runs.** Sit rep ran on the formation 9/15 (three passes; three blocking findings caught by the script reviewer and fixed in parallel) and again 9/16 (one round, no re-runs, 212k specialist tokens: 48k RACK · 90k INDEX · 74k WATCH; the main line read two digests). Oscar Mike ran 9/15 on close.py + NOTE on haiku (71k haiku tokens on a 78 KB transcript).
